incidents.vector: DOJ unsealed a 2024 indictment charging three St. Petersburg-based Russian nationals who allegedly ran the Media Land and ML.Cloud bulletproof hosting services, supplying criminals with infrastructure to deliver malware, ransomware, phishing and brute-force platforms.
incidents.impact: The hosting operations facilitated attacks on critical infrastructure in 21 U.S. states and several countries causing over $62M in losses; the State Department offered up to $10M for information and the U.S., UK and Australia had already sanctioned the trio and both companies in November 2025.

incidents.vector: Members of an English-speaking cybercrime collective breached TfL's network in 2024 using social engineering, SIM-swapping and stolen credentials, coordinating via Telegram and a shared workspace.
incidents.impact: Two members (aged 20 and 18) were sentenced to 5.5 years each; the 2024 attack cost TfL £29M ($39M) in recovery, downed 148 internal systems, forced in-person password resets for 27,000 staff, and exposed Oyster refund customer data.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the servers of a major Japanese refrigerated-logistics operator, forcing it to disconnect key systems to contain the intrusion.
incidents.impact: Frozen and refrigerated shipments across 140 distribution centers were disrupted, leaving 1,300+ KFC Japan outlets short of ingredients and causing shortages at Kura Sushi, Aeon and other chains; some affected servers held personal data still under investigation.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social-engineering lures delivered via malvertising and SEO trick users into running commands that install the ACR infostealer through WebDAV/rundll32 loaders and MSHTA-launched obfuscated PowerShell with steganographic payloads.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Defender Experts observed two prevalent intrusion chains from late April to mid-June 2026 stealing browser credentials, session tokens and sensitive documents, enabling account compromise and follow-on cloud intrusion.

incidents.victim: Users across the U.S. and Europe
incidents.vector: A Russian-speaking crew used ClickFix social engineering and trojanized software installers (MobaXterm, Zoom, WebEx, DBeaver) to deploy the Python-based 'Starland' RAT and a bespoke PowerShell C2 implant.
incidents.impact: The malware steals browser credentials and cryptocurrency wallets and enables follow-on payloads (CastleStealer, Remcos); Cisco Talos reports predominant impact in the U.S. with additional victims in Germany, Romania and Venezuela.

incidents.vector: Attackers chained two zero-days (CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410) in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances to move from no access to full system compromise, exploiting them roughly three weeks before patches shipped.
incidents.impact: Rapid7 observed active exploitation from June 22 with ransomware as the likely goal; CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and SonicWall urged immediate patching and compromise hunting on fewer than 5,000 exposed units.

incidents.vector: An international network ran roughly 24 call centers with 700+ staff posing as financial advisers, grooming victims over weeks before steering them into fake cryptocurrency trading platforms showing fictitious returns.
incidents.impact: Dutch police dismantled the network, which allegedly generated over €100M/month since 2021 (Dutch victims alone lost ~€25M); the alleged mastermind was arrested at a Polish airport and extradited, with five further arrests across Europe.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited elevation-of-privilege zero-days in on-prem SharePoint Server (CVE-2026-56164) and Active Directory Federation Services (CVE-2026-56155) ahead of patches.
incidents.impact: Microsoft's record July Patch Tuesday shipped 600+ fixes addressing three zero-days, at least two confirmed exploited in the wild; CVE-2026-56164 was added to CISA's KEV catalog, and a publicly disclosed BitLocker bypass was also patched.

incidents.vector: Actors scan for internet-facing routers running SNMP with default community strings, then use SNMP set-requests to copy device configs and exfiltrate them via TFTP, occasionally exploiting older Cisco flaws and Smart Install.
incidents.impact: A joint advisory from roughly 20 Five Eyes and European agencies detailed a decade-plus FSB campaign opportunistically compromising poorly configured networking devices across communications, defense, energy, government and other sectors worldwide.

incidents.vector: NetNut bundled software onto consumer devices such as smart TVs and streaming boxes, turning them into always-on residential proxy nodes without meaningful consent to populate the 'Popa' botnet of at least two million devices.
incidents.impact: The FBI and IRS-CI seized hundreds of domains and replaced NetNut's homepage with a seizure banner; the proxy network had been rented out for mass scraping, ad fraud and account-takeover abuse.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused unprotected pre-production release branches in four core AsyncAPI GitHub repos, pushing malicious commits that triggered GitHub Actions to harvest publishing tokens and ship five trojanized npm packages carrying a remote-access trojan.
incidents.impact: The backdoored packages fetch a second-stage RAT from IPFS on install, establishing persistence and exfiltrating GitHub, npm, SSH, cloud, Kubernetes and CI/CD credentials; the campaign shares lineage with a June compromise of Red Hat's npm namespace.

incidents.victim: U.S. businesses, hospitals and municipal governments
incidents.vector: Operators sold a no-logs 'bulletproof' VPN service (First VPN Service / 1VPNS) that ransomware groups used to hide attack origins and manage stolen data, alongside 'cryptors' to disguise ransomware from security tools.
incidents.impact: OFAC, with the UK FCDO, sanctioned the 1VPNS entity, its administrator and a cryptor seller following a May 2026 European/FBI takedown of the infrastructure; ransomware using these services caused billions in losses to U.S. victims.

incidents.victim: UK Foreign Office (FCDO), embassies and local councils
incidents.vector: Credentials for firewall and VPN servers were harvested during the 'FortiBleed' campaign, in which a threat actor stole credentials from nearly 80,000 Fortinet devices.
incidents.impact: Stolen firewall and VPN credentials for the Foreign Office, British embassies and some UK local councils are being offered for sale as a single archive for $60,000.

incidents.victim: CISA (U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor published 844 MB of internal data — including AWS GovCloud admin credentials and a CSV of plaintext logins for dozens of internal systems — to a public GitHub repo that sat exposed for roughly six months.
incidents.impact: Admin keys to three AWS GovCloud servers and dozens of internal credentials were exposed; CISA rotated keys after notification and its logs indicated no mission or customer data was accessed, but the postmortem highlighted slow response and contractor access controls.

incidents.vector: Mass automated scanning and exploitation of dozens of known CMS and plugin vulnerabilities (unauthenticated file upload, RCE, SSRF, deserialization) across WordPress plugins, Craft CMS and Joomla to deploy webshells.
incidents.impact: The ACSC issued a 'critical' alert after compromised web servers were used for defacement, credential capture, malware distribution to visitors and as pivots for broader network compromise, hitting many small and medium Australian businesses.
